name: HxGN Alix
description: HxGN Alix is a 2024 industrial AI assistant from Hexagon that sits inside HxGN EAM and related Asset Lifecycle Intelligence products rather than acting as a generic public chatbot. The product is positioned as a secure, domain-tuned assistant that uses private LLM infrastructure, retrieves information from product workflows and connected industrial systems, and answers questions about features, codes, processes, regulations, and specifications. Hexagon also exposes code-generation help and workflow guidance, which makes it closer to an engineering RAG layer over enterprise asset data than a standalone search box. Public launch materials show it first in EAM with broader portfolio rollout afterward, so the current status is a deployed production assistant with expanding product coverage.

name: Siemens Industrial Copilot for Engineering
description: Siemens Industrial Copilot for Engineering is a 2024 production assistant aimed at automation engineers working in TIA Portal rather than a general enterprise chatbot. Siemens positions it as a generative AI layer that can search engineering documentation, answer workflow questions, and generate Structured Control Language code directly into the engineering environment. Public rollout notes also describe support for screen and visualization generation and cite adoption in battery-machine engineering at thyssenkrupp Automation Engineering. The architecture combines Siemens domain knowledge and industrial controls context with Azure OpenAI models, so the product functions as engineering RAG plus code generation over Siemens software, project assets, and automation knowledge. The current status is deployed production with continuing expansion across the Siemens copilot family.

name: Siemens Industrial Copilot for Operations
description: Siemens Industrial Copilot for Operations is the shop-floor companion in the Siemens copilot family, aimed at machine operators and maintenance staff who need grounded answers from machine context rather than generic web chat. Siemens describes it as an assistant for machine operation, maintenance, error handling, shift support, and performance optimization, with on-prem deployment plans to preserve data sovereignty. Public materials also connect it to Industrial Edge and to time-series analysis features in drivetrain and asset-monitoring workflows. In practice, that makes it an engineering RAG layer over operational data, manuals, alarms, and service knowledge, with natural-language interaction replacing part of the usual hunt through HMIs, logs, and documentation. The current status is deployed production with active portfolio expansion.

name: FactoryTalk Design Studio Copilot
description: FactoryTalk Design Studio Copilot is Rockwell Automation's 2024 generative AI assistant inside its browser-based automation engineering environment. Official product and documentation pages position it as a workflow assistant for PLC and control-system design: users can ask natural-language questions, generate ladder logic and other code artifacts, request explanations of existing project elements, and troubleshoot design problems without leaving the SaaS workspace. Rockwell also states that conversations are private to the organization and are not used to train Azure OpenAI or Rockwell AI models, which matters for engineering IP. Because it is embedded in Design Studio with versioned projects and product context, the tool functions as an industrial engineering RAG and code-generation layer rather than a standalone chatbot. The current status is deployed production.

name: ABB Ability Genix Copilot
description: ABB Ability Genix Copilot is a 2024 generative AI assistant layered on top of ABB's Genix industrial analytics suite. ABB presents it as a context-aware industrial copilot that turns large volumes of asset, process, and operations data into actionable guidance for engineers and operators instead of forcing users to navigate dashboards and siloed applications manually. Launch and product materials emphasize use in energy, utilities, and other asset-heavy industries, and ABB also highlights an LLM-agnostic design so customers are not locked to a single model provider. The related Genix APM Copilot focuses on predictive maintenance and asset performance workflows, which makes the product family a strong example of engineering RAG over industrial telemetry, historian-style data, and maintenance knowledge. The current status is deployed production.

name: Schneider Electric Industrial Copilot
description: Schneider Electric Industrial Copilot is the company's generative assistant for open, software-defined industrial automation workflows. Public launch materials tie it to EcoStruxure Automation Expert and describe it as a tool that helps engineers create validated control applications and code more quickly, while later announcements extend that framing to configuration and documentation tasks for manufacturers. Schneider's messaging emphasizes a closed-loop workflow across engineering teams and tools rather than a generic question-answer bot, which places the product squarely in the engineering RAG and copilot category. The Microsoft partnership and Azure AI integration provide the language-model layer, while Schneider contributes automation context, runtime integration, and edge-oriented deployment patterns. The current status is deployed production with ongoing expansion into more agentic manufacturing workflows.

name: AVEVA Industrial AI Assistant
description: AVEVA Industrial AI Assistant is AVEVA's natural-language assistant for engineering and industrial information retrieval across CONNECT and Unified Engineering workflows. AVEVA first previewed the product in 2024 and then expanded it into the 2026 Unified Engineering release as part of a broader AI stack for capital projects. Vendor materials describe it as a virtual subject matter expert that can interrogate project engineering work, surface scattered information, answer workflow questions, and capture product-usage knowledge for reuse by teams. Because it is embedded in AVEVA's data-centric engineering environment and linked to multidisciplinary project information, the assistant behaves like engineering RAG over design data, documents, and operational context, rather than generic search. The current status is deployed production with broader AI tooling around it, including generative and predictive design assistants.

name: MATLAB AI Chat Playground
description: MATLAB AI Chat Playground is MathWorks' public preview assistant for MATLAB-centered technical computing questions. The product is explicitly targeted at science, engineering, and MATLAB workflows rather than open-domain chat, and the release history shows a January 2025 upgrade that added retrieval-augmented generation to improve relevance and accuracy. MathWorks also frames it as a tool for generating draft MATLAB code, explaining code, and answering questions about MATLAB and related products, which makes it a domain-grounded engineering chat interface over product knowledge and documentation. Because it is still described as experimental, it sits earlier on the maturity curve than fully commercial copilots, but it is a concrete, production-hosted example of engineering RAG customized for simulation, controls, data analysis, and numerical computing users.

name: MATLAB Copilot
description: MATLAB Copilot is MathWorks' production generative AI assistant embedded directly in the MATLAB desktop environment. Launch materials for Release 2025b describe a grounded assistant that can answer questions using MathWorks documentation and real-world code examples, autocomplete or generate MATLAB code from natural-language requests, explain unfamiliar code, clarify errors, add comments, and generate starter tests. That combination makes it more than a generic code chatbot: it is an engineering RAG and code-completion layer tuned to numerical computing, modeling, controls, signal processing, and adjacent technical workflows that dominate MATLAB usage. MathWorks also emphasizes that end-user submitted data is not used to train AI models, which is relevant for proprietary engineering work. The current status is deployed production.

name: Simulink Copilot
description: Simulink Copilot is MathWorks' 2026 assistant for Model-Based Design workflows inside the Simulink environment. Product documentation describes a grounded chat interface that uses the open model plus relevant MathWorks documentation and resources to answer questions, locate model components, and explain models and errors. It also helps resolve simulation and code-generation failures by suggesting likely causes and fixes, which is a narrower but more engineering-specific use case than generic coding chat. In practice, this makes Simulink Copilot a RAG layer over model structure, documentation, and development context for controls, embedded systems, and systems engineering teams. Because it ships as part of the formal 2026a release and licensed copilot stack, its current status is deployed production rather than experimental preview.

name: Polyspace Copilot
description: Polyspace Copilot is MathWorks' generative AI assistant for static-analysis and coding-standards workflows around C and C++ verification. Product pages and documentation describe a chat interface integrated with the Polyspace as You Code plugin in Visual Studio Code, where the assistant explains findings, answers questions grounded in MathWorks documentation, and suggests code changes for defects or standards violations such as MISRA C, MISRA C++, and CERT C/C++. That makes it a specialized engineering RAG system focused on software assurance artifacts rather than open-ended programming help. Because the assistant is tied to the user's local codebase and Polyspace findings, it can produce far more targeted explanations than a generic coding model. The current status is public preview because MathWorks still describes the standalone product as beta.

name: Bentley Copilot
description: Bentley Copilot is Bentley Systems' context-aware assistant for infrastructure engineering applications. Public announcements around Infrastructure AI and new application rollouts describe a copilot that guides users through workflows, surfaces relevant documents, and can make changes to models, with added spatial awareness so it understands relationships between design elements. That makes it more than an enterprise search layer: Bentley is grounding the assistant in engineering models, documents, and application state across its infrastructure software stack. The result is a design-oriented RAG and action assistant aimed at civil, transportation, and construction users who need workflow guidance tied to real project context. Because Bentley has framed the new generation of applications as limited-availability rollouts and early-access programs, the current status is public preview rather than broad mature deployment.

name: Honeywell Forge Production Intelligence AI Assistant
description: Honeywell Forge Production Intelligence AI Assistant is a 2025 generative assistant added to Honeywell's production-monitoring stack for industrial operators and plant managers. Honeywell positions it as part of the Forge Production Intelligence release, where the assistant helps automate tasks and troubleshoot problems while being grounded in performance monitoring and production context. That placement matters: this is not a generic enterprise chatbot bolted onto a dashboard, but an operations-focused RAG layer over Honeywell's plant software, telemetry, and workflow knowledge. It sits alongside the broader Honeywell Forge portfolio, which already combines analytics and domain data across industrial and utility settings. The current status is deployed production, with Honeywell using the assistant to make routine troubleshooting and operational analysis more conversational and faster for plant teams.

name: OpenBOM AI Agent
description: OpenBOM AI Agent is a 2025 product-data assistant built on top of OpenBOM's cloud PDM and PLM platform. OpenBOM frames it as an invisible engineering workflow assistant that understands files and product data, engages with BOM information through natural interaction, and helps teams uncover insights without forcing them into a new standalone interface. Related OpenBOM materials tie the agent and support assistant to documentation retrieval, product-memory ideas, and MCP-based integrations, so the product is best understood as engineering RAG over bills of materials, CAD-linked metadata, inventory, and digital-thread records. That makes it relevant for hardware and manufacturing teams that want conversational access to product structure and change context rather than generic knowledge search. The current status is public preview with ongoing beta-style expansion.

name: Aras AI Assistant
description: Aras AI Assistant is a 2025 PLM assistant for Aras Innovator SaaS that combines conversational access with AI-assisted search across structured and unstructured product data. Aras documentation explicitly states that the assistant is built on retrieval-augmented generation, using documentation, training materials, and other Aras digital content to keep responses grounded. The press release broadens that positioning from documentation help to product data and PLM business processes, highlighting faster access to engineering documents, design files, and critical lifecycle information. That makes the assistant a strong engineering RAG example for digital-thread environments where users need answers tied to configuration, documents, and process state rather than public web knowledge. The current status is deployed production within the Aras SaaS platform.

name: OpenSite+
description: OpenSite+ is Bentley Systems' AI-powered site design application for civil and land-development workflows. Bentley positions it as the first engineering application in its new Infrastructure AI stack and markets it as design software with a built-in copilot, automated drawing production, integrated drainage, and rapid layout exploration. Public materials claim major schedule compression for site planning and emphasize that the software is data-centric and digital-twin aware, rather than a chat layer disconnected from model context. Because Bentley also describes OpenSite+ as featuring Bentley Copilot, the product combines generative layout assistance with engineering RAG and workflow guidance tied to model state and project documents. The current status is public preview or limited availability, which matches Bentley's staged rollout language for its new AI-native applications.

name: Plataine AI Agents
description: Plataine AI Agents are manufacturing-focused assistants built on top of Plataine's AI and IIoT production-optimization stack. Plataine markets the suite as a set of domain-specific agents that automate complex planning, scheduling, material-management, procurement, and production-response tasks while connecting to legacy systems, sensors, and enterprise applications. Related product pages also describe AI-based digital assistants that provide recommendations and predictions to managers and staff in real time, so the offering fits the engineering RAG and operational-copilot theme even though it is aimed at factory execution rather than CAD. The strongest fit is in composite and advanced manufacturing environments where production knowledge, machine state, and material constraints need to be surfaced conversationally and acted on quickly. The current status is deployed production.

name: Chat with Proficy
description: Chat with Proficy is GE Vernova's generative AI assistant concept for Proficy Smart Factory workflows. The public webinar description presents it as a way to chat with Proficy using gen AI to support the connected worker, which implies natural-language access to plant context instead of navigation through multiple manufacturing software screens. While GE Vernova's public materials stop short of a full standalone product page, the framing is still useful for this database because it shows how industrial software vendors are turning MES, historian, and smart-factory data into conversational engineering interfaces. Relative to more mature copilots, this entry sits earlier in the lifecycle, closer to a previewed capability or solution concept than a broadly packaged commercial assistant. The current status is therefore best described as research prototype or public demonstration.

name: Glean Chat
description: Glean Chat is the conversational layer on top of Glean's enterprise search and knowledge graph stack. Glean launched it as a chat assistant grounded exclusively in up-to-date company knowledge rather than model pretraining alone, with permission-aware retrieval and later additions such as code search and assistant access from desktop quick chat. That makes it relevant for engineering organizations that need answers stitched together from GitHub, docs, tickets, wikis, and internal conversations without breaking access controls. While it is not limited to engineering, it is widely positioned as a secure work assistant over enterprise knowledge, which maps cleanly onto engineering RAG use cases such as design-document lookup, internal API search, and troubleshooting. The current status is deployed production.

name: NotebookLM Enterprise
description: NotebookLM Enterprise is Google's source-grounded notebook and chat environment for organizations. Google documents it as an enterprise generative AI service that works over user-provided sources such as Google Docs, Slides, PDFs, URLs, markdown, pasted text, YouTube links, and audio files, rather than relying only on general model memory. That source-first design is why it is relevant to engineering RAG: teams can drop in specifications, manuals, design reviews, reports, and standards, then ask follow-up questions or request summaries that stay anchored to the uploaded corpus. It is not purpose-built for engineering software, but it has become a practical pattern for design and research teams that need quick retrieval and synthesis over bounded technical source sets. The current status is deployed production for enterprise users.

name: Perplexity Enterprise Pro
description: Perplexity Enterprise Pro extends Perplexity's answer-engine model into organizational retrieval over both the web and internal data. Official help and onboarding pages describe file connectors, GitHub integration, SharePoint and OneDrive access, Google Drive support, and Snowflake search, which means answers can blend external references with company documents and repositories. For engineering teams, that makes the product useful for specification lookup, standards review, design-reference search, and cross-checking internal source files against external technical material in a single conversational flow. It remains a general-purpose enterprise tool rather than an engineering-specific platform, but the combination of citations, connectors, and internal knowledge search makes it a practical engineering RAG assistant. The current status is deployed production as an enterprise offering.

name: ChatGPT Enterprise
description: ChatGPT Enterprise is OpenAI's managed enterprise workspace for organizational AI use, including engineering knowledge retrieval and workflow assistants. Official product and help pages emphasize enterprise security controls, company knowledge, connectors to tools such as GitHub, SharePoint, Google Drive, and Box, plus the ability to create custom GPTs for internal workflows. Those features are what make it relevant to this database: engineering teams can use the platform as a bounded RAG layer over specs, design documents, source repositories, and internal procedures rather than only as an open-ended chatbot. It is still a general enterprise platform rather than a domain-specific engineering product, but the combination of connectors, projects, deep research, and customizable assistants makes it a common foundation for CAD-spec lookup and internal engineering support bots. The current status is deployed production.

name: Dassault Systemes Virtual Companions
description: Dassault Systemes Virtual Companions are AI-powered experts introduced on the 3DEXPERIENCE platform in 2026 under the names Aura, Leo, and Marie. Dassault positions them as industrial companions that help, teach, and work through natural conversation while reasoning with Industry World Models and orchestrating actions across disciplines. That framing puts them beyond a document-search chatbot: the system is intended to combine conversational interaction with platform context, industrial know-how, and process orchestration for complex engineering and manufacturing work. For this database, the relevance is that they represent a major vendor attempt to build engineering RAG and agentic assistance directly into a digital-thread platform, with model grounding in industrial context rather than generic office data. The current status is deployed production or early commercial rollout on 3DEXPERIENCE.

name: OpenBOM AI Support Agent
description: OpenBOM AI Support Agent is the documentation-grounded assistant that OpenBOM surfaced directly in its workspace for users who need help navigating product-data workflows. OpenBOM describes it as a smart assistant that understands questions contextually, retrieves information from official documentation, and returns clear step-by-step guidance. Compared with the broader OpenBOM AI Agent vision, this support-focused assistant is more explicitly a production RAG tool over manuals, help content, and workflow knowledge. That makes it a strong fit for engineering-chat databases because it shows how PLM and BOM vendors are embedding support retrieval directly into daily work rather than forcing users to leave the application and search separate documentation silos. The current status is deployed production within the OpenBOM platform.

name: OpenUtilities Substation+
description: OpenUtilities Substation+ is Bentley Systems' AI-powered substation design application, released through an early-access style rollout as part of the company's new Infrastructure AI portfolio. Bentley describes it as a connected environment for substation design with real-time collaboration, digital-twin context, and AI-powered capabilities, rather than a static CAD tool. Like OpenSite+, it sits in the family of new applications that feature Bentley Copilot-style workflow guidance and document surfacing, which makes it relevant to engineering RAG and chat use cases even though the end output is design content rather than text alone. For utilities and power-engineering teams, the product represents a move toward conversational and context-aware design assistance tied to live project data. The current status is public preview based on Bentley's early-access positioning.
